core_obligations: Observe that the statement makes sense because Z x_X Y is a closed subscheme of Y, and that the class c(Z -> X, N) cap [Y]_n lies in the degree n - r part (proof lines 12145-12147).

Reduce to the generic point of a single component: since dim(Z x_X Y) <= n - r, the group CH_{n-r}(Z x_X Y) is freely generated by the cycle classes of the irreducible components W of that dimension (proof lines 12148-12151).

At the generic point xi of such a component, get dim(O_{Y,xi}) = r from the dimension hypothesis, and use that N has rank r and N-dual surjects onto C_{Z/X} to see that the ideal sheaf of Z x_X Y in Y is locally generated by r elements (proof lines 12152-12157).

Combine Cohen-Macaulayness with the r generators to conclude that I_xi is generated by a regular sequence, spread this to an open neighbourhood V of xi, and finish on V by the fundamental-class lemma because the excess normal sheaf vanishes there (proof lines 12158-12170).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the generic point of a top dimensional component through the free generation of the Chow group (proof lines 12145-12151).
Produce a regular sequence generating the ideal at that point from the rank and Cohen-Macaulay hypotheses (proof lines 12152-12165).
Apply the fundamental-class lemma on the neighbourhood where the excess sheaf vanishes (proof lines 12166-12170).
difficulty_reason: For a virtual normal sheaf N of a closed subscheme Z of X, a morphism Y -> X locally of finite type, and integers r, n, the lemma asserts that under four hypotheses - N locally free of rank r, every component of Y of dimension n, dim(Z x_X Y) <= n - r, and Cohen-Macaulayness of O_{Y,xi} at every point xi of Z x_X Y of dimension n - r - the Gysin class c(Z -> X, N) caps [Y]_n to [Z x_X Y]_{n-r} (statement lines 12127-12142). The proof reduces the global statement to a local one: since the target has dimension at most n - r its Chow group is freely generated by the components W of dimension n - r, so it suffices to work at the generic point xi of such a W (proof lines 12145-12151). There, dim(O_{Y,xi}) = r by the dimension hypothesis and, because N has rank r and its dual surjects onto the conormal sheaf, the ideal of Z is locally cut out by r equations; combined with Cohen-Macaulayness this makes I_xi generated by a regular sequence, which spreads to an open neighbourhood V of xi (proof lines 12152-12165). On V the excess normal sheaf vanishes, so the fundamental-class lemma applies and gives the required identity (proof lines 12166-12170). Turning the four hypotheses into a regular sequence at the generic point of each top dimensional component is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
